Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

require verb

also need, call for, be needed, requirement, demand

classical

Caes. BG 6.34: magnam rēs dīligentiam requīrēbat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 64: virtūtēs animī magnae et multae requīruntur (Lewis & Short)

requīrō, requīrere, requīsīvī, requīsītum

verb, third conjugation

need, require; miss

Of what a task or a situation calls for; in the passive, “to be required”.

Other words

  • opus est — there is need of; it is needed

    impersonal: the dative of the person, the thing needed in the ablative or the nominative · classical · Cato Agr. 14: quae opus sunt; Ter. Ad. 996: quid factō opus est

    The everyday way to say “need”: mihi opus est librō or liber mihi opus est, I need a book; with a participle in the ablative, quid factō opus est?, what needs doing? (Lewis & Short, s.v. opus).

  • postulō, postulāre, postulāvī, postulātum — call for, demand

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. And. 189: aliōs mōrēs postulat

    Of a person or a situation that asks for something.

  • egeō, egēre, eguī — need, be in want of

    verb, second conjugation, with the ablative or the genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 17: egetque exercitātiōne nōn parvā

Examples

  • Nunc hic diēs aliam vītam affert, aliōs mōrēs postulat.

    Now this day brings a different life with it and calls for different ways.Ter. And. 189

  • magnum opus est egetque exercitātiōne nōn parvā

    it is a great task and needs no small practiceCic. Lael. 17

  • Plūs scīs quid factō opus est.

    You know better what needs to be done.Ter. Ad. 996

See also involve, practice, lack.

SourcesLewis & Short: requiro · Lewis & Short: opus · Lewis & Short: postulo · Lewis & Short: egeo
